title: Bose–Einstein condensation at positive temperature in the dilute hard-sphere gas
coverage:
Read all of the LaTeX in build/sections (introduction, setup, energy, spatial, slab, bridges, groups, lattice, comparison, conclusion). Checks made:
(1) Purification identity: Phi = Z^{-1/2} B^sym_{beta/2}, the slab-law normalization, and the formula B_occ = V^{-1} ∫|∫Phi dx|^2.
(2) Cell-affinity identity B_occ = V^{-2} sum Aff(P_vw,Q_vw).
(3) Tag normalization: sum over groups of P̂_g ≤ N Phi^2, which gives the 1/D factor. Also data processing for affinity under projection.
(4) The Hölder (4,4,2) common-measure lemma.
(5) Cancellation lemma: the exact likelihood Z_S H_S / Y_S, the Z_U/Z_S/Y_S insertion bounds, the H_S H_T integral ≤ Y_FS Y_FT G^{|S∩T|}, and the final a^{-2c} bound with |C_S|+|C_T| ≤ 2J_R.
(6) Label-match average, the kappa/2 + kappa/2 split, the tag-splitting and observation-kernel Cauchy–Schwarz step, and the c_* bookkeeping (G_D/(4DC_2) ≥ l/(32MC_2), times υ).
(7) Energy section: cube and close-neighbour constants in outline, the Bose entropy bound, F_j/j monotonicity via strong subadditivity, and the insertion frame bound.
(8) Low-count and close-count diagonal-tilt arguments, including the ODE for L(λ) and the exponential Markov steps.
(9) Marked-kernel geometric mean (it reduces to C g_{3δ} uniformly in t). Trace sandwich: the derivative identity, the exterior-power log-majorization giving all q>0, Schatten–Hölder, and the colour-sector decomposition with field and removal costs. Smallness and visitor/diameter/irregularity choices in the certificate proof.
(10) Bridge mesh sums (r^3 m_t ≤ Ctr, and r D^{3γ}/sqrt(h0) = α D^{-1/4}), the Gaussian packing bound, the G density bound for Π_i^U, the e_D formula, and the group-supply hypergeometric/union bound.
(11) Lattice: the rejection probability, detour charge and animal expansion, the choice of κ and p0 depending only on R, and the υ count.
(12) Physical rescaling: s→s_∞, D→D_∞ > 2D_*, Dr→α0, DT→1/4.
The parameter order (R, p0, κ → α0, ℓ, θ, b → p1, H1, t → G → M → D_* → K) has no circular dependence.
Taken on trust or only spot-checked: details of the dyadic skeleton conditional-density bound, Timár/Kesten boundary connectivity, and the Feynman–Kac exhaustion argument.
main_claim: For every exclusion distance a>0 there is ρ_*(a)>0 such that, for each fixed density 0<ρ<ρ_*(a), some fixed temperature T(a,ρ)>0 (independent of volume) gives the canonical hard-sphere Gibbs state on the torus a constant-orbital occupation fraction ⟨u0,γ^(1)u0⟩/N with positive liminf in the thermodynamic limit. In scaled units this is Theorem 2.1: B_occ ≥ c_* for D ≥ D_*, 0<T≤1/D, and K large.
